Q: Node in Jenkins is offline although agent is connected in server A:

Your CMD says it's connected and the Jenkins logs show the intial handshake but the node never goes to "Online". The issue is likely not in the Jenkins configuration but the underlying resource limits that your infra team might have changed(capped). This is probably because when your infra team fixed the slowness they might have adjusted the load balancer timeouts or MTU sizes.

[JNLP4-connect connection from <server ip info>:54036] APP SEND: 1,483 bytes
in the above log, this is very close to the standard MTU limit of 1500 bytes. Due to a new network encapsulation adding overhead, these packets might get fragmented. This would still allow the handshake (smaller packets) but the heavy data exchange (export/unexport) fails.

Probably the infra team did some new firewall rules for the enabled Jenkins port(50000 or a random higher port)

Q: Get angular-cli to ng serve over HTTPS A:

You can use

--ssl

or

"serve": {
          "builder": "@angular-devkit/build-angular:dev-server",
          "options": {
            "browserTarget": "someapp:build",
            "ssl": true
          },

and an ssl cert will automatically be generated for you.

You'll also need to import the cert into your Trusted Root Certificates. To do this, click the cert error at top of Chrome then:

  1. Click certificate (invalid)
  2. Click the Details tab
  3. Click Copy to File...
  4. next next finish and export it somewhere.
  5. start-> run-> inetcpl.cpl
  6. click Content tab
  7. click Certificates
  8. click Trusted Root Certication Authorities tab
  9. Click Import button
  10. Import the cert
  11. Re-run ng serve --ssl

Be aware, the cert only lasts one month. At the end of that month you'll struggle to find a solution but I've already been through this and here is the fix

Q: how can I regexp match a string containing only isolated instances of a character among other characters? A:

Using any POSIX awk:

$ awk 'sub(/.*CL[0-9]+__/,"") && sub(/__.*/,"")' file
SOC_PM_DF_CSTATE_REGR

or any POSIX sed:

$ sed -En 's/__/\n/g; s/.*CL[0-9]+\n([^\n]+).*/\1/p' file
SOC_PM_DF_CSTATE_REGR

Q: How do I handle read system calls for HPC? A:

the problem is with reading the data because system calls are expensive for computation time

How do you know that?

You've actually measured the time spent performing IO? And demonstrated that how you do that IO actually matters performance-wise? If you haven't done that, you're engaging in premature optimization.

Q: HDLBits problem ece241_2014_q7a. Simulation of my solution is not correspondent with reference A:

The HDLBits site is fine for only the most basic logic designs, but it is worthless when it comes to designs like the one in this example. Here are some specific problems associated with this example on the HDLBits site:

  • We can not see the Verilog code for the count4 design.
  • We can not see the Verilog code for the testbench that the site used.
  • We can not view waveforms of internal signals to debug your failing simulation.
  • The description of the design is ambiguous. It is not clear if the enable input is synchronous to the clock or not. The bottom waveforms seems to indicate that it is asynchronous. If so, then there would be simulation race conditions, leading to unpredictable results.

I recommend abandoning this approach. You should create your own count4 design Verilog code and your own testbench Verilog code to verfiy its functionality. Run simulations outside of the HDLBits site on another simulator and dump waveforms of all internal signals.

Then you can proceed to create the count-12 design and simulate that.

I have observed problems with the site.

Also, this line has illegal syntax:

case({{reset|(Q>11)},enable})VerilogVerilog

The VerilogVerilog should not be there.
